# SlopStopper

> A Python CLI plus GitHub Actions workflows that run security, hygiene and
> reliability checks on every PR. One command to install into any repo.
> It stops AI-generated slop reaching production. People, agents and CI run
> every check with the same `task ss:*` command.

SlopStopper is a quality suite you install into your own repo with one
command. Every check runs the same way on your machine and in CI, and reports
into the pull request. This site is built and deployed with the same suite.

Slop is code and docs produced faster than anyone reads them: a pasted key,
a function nobody can follow, a doc naming a task that no longer exists, a
page that fails contrast. Each check catches one kind and exits 0 when the
repo passed, 1 when it failed, 2 when the check could not run.

To try one check, or to install the whole suite into a repo:

```sh
pipx install slopstopper-cli
slopstopper checks list                # every check
slopstopper doctor                     # which external tools are missing
slopstopper run hygiene:docs-size      # one check; report in .ss/reports/

# the suite: pinned CLI, ss-*.yml workflows, task ss:* commands, pre-push hook
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hungovercoders/slopstopper/main/install.sh | bash
# an API or a library: --profile api / --profile library
```

Needs Python; the installer also needs mise. Settings live in
`.slopstopper.yml`. In Claude Code, the installed `slopstopper-install` and
`slopstopper-triage` skills do the install and fix a red check.

## Site

- [Home](https://slopstopper.dev/): what SlopStopper is, the two ways to install it, and the four loops of checks
- [Features](https://slopstopper.dev/features.html): every check by loop (security, reliability, hygiene, operational), the workflow behind each, the profiles, and what the pull request feedback looks like
- [Tools](https://slopstopper.dev/tools.html): the tool behind each check: Semgrep, OWASP ZAP, Trivy, Gitleaks, Playwright, axe-core, Lighthouse CI, and the pieces every install carries
- [Learn](https://slopstopper.dev/learn.html): a course of twenty-one short lessons, one check at a time, run against a demo repo the CLI writes; each lesson is a page under /learn/, listed below
- [Docs](https://slopstopper.dev/docs.html): the reference docs as pages under /docs/, listed below: what every check enforces and how to fix what it finds, installing and tuning the suite, the architecture
- [Feedback](https://slopstopper.dev/feedback.html): report a bug or request a check
- [Privacy](https://slopstopper.dev/privacy.html): what the site collects (nothing of its own), what Cloudflare keeps as the host, and which other services the pages reach

## The course

One lesson per page, in order; each one's goal is its summary.

<!-- learn:begin -->
- [Lesson 0: What slop is, and the five loops](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/00-what-slop-is.html): Say what slopstopper stops and how, so every later lesson has a frame to sit in.
- [Lesson 1: Install slopstopper into a repo](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/01-install.html): Install the suite into a repo, pick a profile, know what every file it wrote is for, and see which checks the repo is now carrying.
- [Lesson 2: Run your first check and read its report](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/02-first-check-complexity.html): Run one check against the demo repo, read the red line and the report it points at, fix what it names, and see it go green. This is the loop every later lesson repeats.
- [Lesson 3: Entry files: the AGENTS.md-first model](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/03-entry-files.html): Say why README.md and AGENTS.md have token budgets, find the demo's README over its budget, and see that the fix is to move content deeper and route it, never to raise the budget.
- [Lesson 4: Docs structure: every doc has a route](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/04-docs-structure.html): Find the doc in the demo that nothing routes to, see why a "see also" link does not count, route it, and understand the hop and line limits.
- [Lesson 5: Docs accuracy and docs size](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/05-docs-accuracy-and-size.html): Find the doc in the demo that describes a command the repo does not have, read the finding, make the doc true, and then read the growth signal the size monitor prints without ever failing a build.
- [Lesson 6: Secrets](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/06-secrets.html): Commit a fake private key to the demo, watch Gitleaks catch it, see why deleting it in a later commit does not help, and learn the fix that does.
- [Lesson 7: Static analysis](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/07-sast.html): Find the one unsafe line in the demo's script, read the finding Semgrep raised for it, and fix the code rather than the rule.
- [Lesson 8: Dependencies and licences](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/08-dependencies.html): Find the pinned package in the demo with a known CVE, read the report's "Fixed In" column, take the fix, and see where the licence gates sit.
- [Lesson 9: Headers and CSP](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/09-headers-and-csp.html): See the headers the demo's host sends, find the Content-Security-Policy relaxation nobody wrote down, document it properly, and then audit an API's CORS headers and fix the commonest mistake.
- [Lesson 10: Dynamic scanning](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/10-dast.html): Serve the demo, run OWASP ZAP against it, read a baseline report, see what the gate accepts and why, and accept one finding with a reason.
- [Lesson 11: Smoke and end-to-end](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/11-smoke-and-e2e.html): Serve the demo, run the two browser checks that prove it works for a visitor, break each one the way a real change would, and read what the browser saw.
- [Lesson 12: Accessibility](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/12-accessibility.html): Audit both of the demo's pages with axe-core, find the one attribute a screen reader depends on that the history page is missing, and fix it.
- [Lesson 13: Core Web Vitals](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/13-core-web-vitals.html): Run Lighthouse against the demo, read the budget it enforces, add one blocking script, and watch the numbers move.
- [Lesson 14: SEO and social share](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/14-seo.html): Audit the tags a search engine and a link preview read, find the one the demo's history page is missing, and see what it would have broken.
- [Lesson 15: Discoverability: robots, sitemap, llms.txt and links](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/15-discoverability.html): Run the four checks that decide whether anyone finds a page, fix the one the demo ships red, and break the other three to see which catches what.
- [Lesson 16: API checks: health, latency and OpenAPI drift](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/16-api-checks.html): Point the three API checks at a small API, see each one fail on its own kind of drift, and understand why they exist alongside the browser checks.
- [Lesson 17: CI: the workflows and the PR feedback loop](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/17-ci.html): Read one check workflow end to end, see that it is the same task line you have been typing, and follow a red check from the Actions log to the pull request comment to the issue it raises on main.
- [Lesson 18: Agents: the install and triage skills](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/18-agents.html): Install the two Claude Code skills into a repo, read how they are shaped, and see how an agent uses them to install the suite or fix a red check without being told the steps.
- [Lesson 19: Profiles and tailoring](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/19-profiles-and-tailoring.html): Switch a repo between the ui, api and library profiles, keep one check a profile drops, and know where the CLI pin lives and how it moves.
- [Lesson 20: Inside slopstopper: add a check](https://slopstopper.dev/learn/20-inside-slopstopper.html): Register a new check in the CLI, let the test suite tell you the other surfaces it must be wired into, and understand the shape every check shares.
<!-- learn:end -->

## Docs

One page per reference doc an adopter reads, by section; each section's index says when to read what. The docs about working on the repository itself are on GitHub, under Source.

<!-- docs:begin -->
- [Runbooks: Runbooks](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/runbooks/index.html): What you do once around the suite: install it into a repo, install the Claude Code skills, move the CLI pin, and, for the project itself, cut a release.
- [Runbooks: Adopting SlopStopper](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/runbooks/install.html): Everything an adopter needs once: prerequisites, the install command, what the installer writes, what each check needs from you, how to run the suite, configure it and move the CLI pin.
- [Runbooks: Install the SlopStopper Claude Code skills](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/runbooks/install-skills.html): Install or refresh the two Claude Code skills on their own, without re-running the whole installer. Where install.sh puts the whole suite into a repo, install-skill.sh writes just the skills.
- [Runbooks: Upgrade the pinned slopstopper-cli](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/runbooks/upgrade-cli.html): Move a repo's pinned slopstopper-cli to a newer release.
- [Hygiene: Hygiene](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/hygiene/index.html): The checks that keep code readable and docs true, for people and for agents: what each enforces, which setting tunes it, and how to fix what it finds.
- [Hygiene: Agentic Documentation Updater](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/hygiene/doc-updater.html): A weekly agent reads what merged, finds the docs that drifted from it, and opens a pull request with the fixes. It runs on GitHub Agentic Workflows (gh-aw) with the GitHub Copilot CLI engine.
- [Security: Security](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/security/index.html): The security checks: what each one looks at, how it blocks, and where to tune it. One page per check; read the one whose trigger matches.
- [Security: API Headers & CORS](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/security/api-headers.html): Audits a JSON API's response headers and CORS policy, where a permissive policy on a credentialed API is a cross-origin data leak.
- [Security: CSP exceptions](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/security/csp-exceptions.html): This file is the single source of truth for every per-path Content-Security-Policy relaxation on the SlopStopper site.
- [Security: Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST)](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/security/dast.html): OWASP ZAP scans your running site, or your API through its OpenAPI spec, for runtime security issues.
- [Security: Licence Inventory](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/security/licences.html): security:licences judges every dependency the lockfiles resolve to against the repo's licence allowlist, so a transitive package under a denied licence cannot sit in the tree unnoticed.
- [Security: Static Application Security Testing (SAST)](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/security/sast.html): Semgrep scans your source code for security bugs and unsafe patterns before they merge.
- [Security: Secrets Detection](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/security/secrets.html): Gitleaks scans your source and your git history for committed credentials, API keys and other secrets.
- [Security: Dependency Vulnerability Scanning](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/security/vulnerability.html): Trivy scans your dependencies for known CVEs.
- [Reliability: Reliability Testing](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/reliability/index.html): The checks that prove the deployed site or API works for a visitor, each run against any reachable URL. Smoke, broken links, API health and API latency are covered below; seven more have a page each.
- [Reliability: Accessibility Monitoring](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/reliability/accessibility.html): axe-core audits every page against WCAG 2.1 AA, on every pull request, push to main and deploy, and daily.
- [Reliability: Core Web Vitals](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/reliability/cwv.html): reliability:cwv runs Lighthouse CI against a URL and fails the build when a page's performance falls below budget. It is the browser-side speed check; API Latency is its analogue for a JSON API.
- [Reliability: E2E Journeys](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/reliability/e2e.html): The E2E check proves a visitor can get around: it drives a browser through the journeys any HTML site offers, without knowing anything about yours.
- [Reliability: llms.txt AI-Discoverability Check](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/reliability/llms-txt.html): Audits your site's /llms.txt, the llmstxt.org map that lets an AI assistant read your key pages without parsing HTML.
- [Reliability: robots.txt Discoverability Check](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/reliability/robots-txt.html): Audits your site's /robots.txt: a stray Disallow: / that would de-index the whole site fails, and a Sitemap: pointer is required. /robots.txt is the Robots Exclusion Protocol file every crawler…
- [Reliability: SEO & Social-Share Metatag Check](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/reliability/seo.html): Asserts the tags a search engine and a link preview read on each page: title, description, canonical, OpenGraph and Twitter Card, with the share image reachable.
- [Reliability: sitemap.xml Completeness + Drift Check](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/reliability/sitemap.html): Crawls your site and cross-checks sitemap.xml against the pages it reaches: a reachable page missing from it, or an entry that 404s, fails.
- [Architecture: Architecture](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/architecture/index.html): How the suite fits together: the CLI, the workflows and the task ss:* commands that call it, the toolchain, and the inner and outer loops the checks run in.
- [Architecture: PR feedback: one summary, compact detail](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/architecture/pr-feedback.html): Every pull request gets one summary comment, and a failing check adds a short comment of its own; this page is why, and the format of each.
- [Architecture: Project-shape profiles](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/architecture/profiles.html): A profile picks the checks that fit a repo's shape: ui for a website, api for a service with no pages, library for a package that serves nothing.
- [Architecture: slopstopper-steward: the org-wide operator](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/architecture/steward.html): slopstopper-steward works across a GitHub organisation: it upgrades every repo that has slopstopper installed and works the issues the checks raised, one pull request each.
- [Support: Support](https://slopstopper.dev/docs/support/index.html): Where to ask a question, report a bug or request a check: an AI assistant first, then an issue on the repository, then a discussion.
<!-- docs:end -->

## Source

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/hungovercoders/slopstopper): source, install.sh and the slopstopper CLI
- [README](https://github.com/hungovercoders/slopstopper/blob/main/README.md): install and usage
- [Course syllabus](https://github.com/hungovercoders/slopstopper/blob/main/docs/learn/README.md): the lessons as markdown, with the episode to follow for each
- [Agent guide](https://github.com/hungovercoders/slopstopper/blob/main/AGENTS.md): what most tasks in the repo need, within ~2k tokens

## For agents

- [slopstopper-install skill](https://github.com/hungovercoders/slopstopper/blob/main/.claude/skills/slopstopper-install/SKILL.md): install SlopStopper into a repo or refresh an existing install
- [slopstopper-triage skill](https://github.com/hungovercoders/slopstopper/blob/main/.claude/skills/slopstopper-triage/SKILL.md): diagnose and fix a failing SlopStopper check
- [slopstopper-steward](https://github.com/hungovercoders/slopstopper-steward): across a GitHub organisation, upgrades every adopter and works the issues the suite raised, one PR each. Each organisation runs its own fork or template copy; [its setup runbook](https://github.com/hungovercoders/slopstopper-steward/blob/main/docs/runbooks/SETUP.md) walks the copy, the GitHub App and the first dry run
